- When sentiment is high (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply +1–2% bias to first 5 forecasts.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently high over 3+ days, model overreacts; apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility by 10–15%.
- In late 30-day horizon (last 5–7 days), model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture tail risk.
